dialogues.speaker: Zamorov
dialogues.text: Who's the face of the theater? Why, the answer is obvious: the incomparable Vodyanitsa, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Zamorov
dialogues.text: Every time Lady Vodyanitsa takes the stage, the cheers are so deafening they nearly bring the roof down. Even the chandeliers are in danger of shattering!

dialogues.speaker: Zamorov
dialogues.text: Just look across the entire Korolevskiy Troupe — is there a single performer more beloved than she is?

dialogues.speaker: Taisia
dialogues.text: Your reasoning is laughably simplistic. Those cheers and screams merely reflect fans imitating their favorite actress. They prove nothing about her popularity.

dialogues.speaker: Taisia
dialogues.text: Odette's admirers, on the other hand, greet her arrival with the same grace and refinement she embodies — with dignified applause.

dialogues.speaker: Taisia
dialogues.text: Such elegance is perfectly in keeping with the troupe's distinguished image. And image, after all, is the most important criterion when deciding who serves as its face.

dialogues.speaker: Taisia
dialogues.text: The answer should therefore be self-evident.

dialogues.speaker: Zamorov
dialogues.text: Your thinking is hopelessly provincial. I'm not sure this conversation can continue.

dialogues.speaker: Taisia
dialogues.text: No matter. I don't believe there's anything left for us to discuss, either.
